requirements.requirement: Wall-hung spice rack with at least three bins
requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row at 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 2,0,0 each fitted with hex-bin-full-div3 (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3) = 3 bins × 3 compartments = 9 spice slots, joined with side-connector-double at both seams.

Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories on the rear face (accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#1,0#4, accessory:0#2,0#4) on slot 4, one per cell, for lift-and-drop mounting on wall screws. Build capped and locked with lockJoints + capOpenFaces (22 printed instances).

finish.summary: Built a horizontal 3-cell spice rack (507×89×384 mm) with three 3-compartment full-depth bins. Each cell carries a keyhole hanger on its back face for wall mounting, cells are joined by double side connectors and locked. Props not placed — compartment size 44 mm wide does not accept the XS pot (64 mm) per PROP_NO_REST; structure alone demonstrates the spice-rack use.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
